title: CoreWeave Shares Rally on Q3 Beat, but Analysts Mostly Hold Ratings and Several Cut Targets
dek: The stock jumped in premarket trading after revenue of $3.66 billion and a raised 2026 outlook, yet Cantor and Stifel slashed their targets and Bernstein says the fundamentals remain the overhang.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Interior of a stock market trading centre with a large display of prices

keyPoints: CoreWeave's third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% year over year, beat analyst estimates of about $3.55 billion, and the company raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $13.0-$13.3 billion (Benzinga).
CNBC reported the shares rose about 13% in premarket trading on Wednesday; Benzinga put the early premarket gain at 16.7%, to $56.85.
Cantor Fitzgerald cut its target from $176 to $100 and kept an Overweight rating; Stifel cut its target from $120 to $60 and kept a Hold (Benzinga).
Deutsche Bank ($125, Buy), Bank of America ($140, Buy) and UBS ($105, Buy) kept bullish ratings; Morgan Stanley ($70, Equal Weight) and Barclays ($105, Equal Weight) stayed neutral (CNBC).
Bernstein's Madison Rezaei said execution is improving but that 'the fundamentals remain the overhang' (CNBC).
body:
CoreWeave's shares rose in premarket trading on Wednesday after the AI cloud provider reported third-quarter results that beat its own guidance and Wall Street's estimates. The rebound, though, has not translated into a wave of upgrades. Several analysts trimmed their price targets, and the sell-side message is that the quarter eased near-term worries without settling the funding question.

## What the quarter showed

CoreWeave reported revenue of $3.66 billion, up 168% from a year earlier and more than $1 billion higher than the prior quarter, according to Benzinga. Chief Executive Michael Intrator called it "a breakout quarter." The company said adjusted operating margins reached double digits a quarter ahead of plan, and it lifted its 2026 revenue range to $13.0-$13.3 billion, from $12.4-$13.2 billion. Management also said it expects to exit the year with an annualized revenue run-rate of $20-$21 billion.

The bigger source of relief for investors was financing. CNBC reported that CoreWeave's five-year credit default swaps had climbed past their October highs ahead of the report, a sign that bondholders saw rising risk. Management paired the results with a more detailed capital plan that leans on contract-backed financing and customer prepayments rather than unsecured debt.

## Analysts split between patience and cuts

The price-target changes were mixed. Benzinga reported that Cantor Fitzgerald's Brett Knoblauch kept an Overweight rating but lowered his target to $100 from $176, while Stifel's Ruben Roy kept a Hold and cut his target to $60 from $120.

Others left their numbers largely in place. Deutsche Bank called the quarter a delivery on "multiple fronts," with a $125 Buy target. Bank of America, at Buy and $140, said funding needs look manageable. Morgan Stanley, at Equal Weight and $70, said it came away "incrementally more positive" on the 2027 financing bridge but wants to see a new delayed-draw term loan completed first.

Not everyone was persuaded. UBS, which kept a Buy and a $105 target, said restoring confidence "may be a multi-quarter fix." Bernstein's Rezaei wrote that the company is maturing but that the fundamentals are still shaky.

## Market read-through

The move was not limited to CoreWeave. 24/7 Wall St. reported that Marvell and Intel each rose about 7% and Taiwan Semiconductor about 4% in early trading, with analysts tying the rally to renewed confidence that AI infrastructure spending will be financed. 24/7 Wall St. also reported that Nvidia gained despite a Baird downgrade on Wednesday over AI spending visibility and CEO uncertainty.

The risk is that the stock's reaction runs ahead of the balance sheet. Interest expense of about $846 million in the quarter, against a company-guided range of $860-$940 million, was slightly better than guidance, but it is still large relative to operating income. Investors will look for detail on the 2027 financing plan and on how quickly backlog converts to revenue.

This is market analysis, not financial advice.

marketImpact.summary: The revenue beat and raised outlook support the growth case, but the price-target cuts from Cantor and Stifel, and the neutral calls from Morgan Stanley and Barclays, show that analysts still treat financing as the main constraint. The premarket gain may fade if the regular session does not confirm it.
marketImpact.timeframe: Wednesday's regular session and the next one or two sessions
